Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

bssd 0.2.0

  • New functions for other published methods for blinded safety data, all computed by numerical integration and returning class bssd_post:
    • exptime_post(): the exposure-time Poisson model of Schnell and Ball (2016) with subject-level event counts and follow-up times.
    • binbeta_post(): the binomial model of Ball and Schnell (2016) with the numbers of enrolled subjects and of subjects with the event.
    • canary_post(): the method of Gould and Wang (2017) for the total event count, with the ratio, the difference or the odds ratio as the metric and a binomial or Poisson likelihood.
    • mapbern_post() and map_beta(): the meta-analytic predictive prior from historical control arms and the mixture likelihood of Brock et al. (2023).
    • multibin_post(): the meta-analysis of several blinded studies of Goren et al. (2020) with a common rate ratio.
  • bdribs_grid() and pooled_ratio(): the contour plots and the pooled randomization ratio of Waterhouse et al. (2022) for BDRIBS.
  • signal_count() gives the smallest event count with a signal for a number of subjects (canary_post() or binbeta_post()), count_oc() the exact probability that the event count reaches it, and elicit_prior() the parameters of a Gamma, Beta or lognormal prior from two quantiles.
  • sim_oc() also runs the models "EXPTIME" and "MAPBERN".
  • The two-dimensional integrals of exptime_post(), binbeta_post(), mapbern_post() and canary_post() (binomial likelihood) locate, for each node of the control parameter, the interval of the second coordinate that holds the conditional posterior mass, and multibin_post() locates the posterior of the log rate ratio on its standardized scale. The results stay accurate when the data conflict with an informative prior of the study drug parameter, and, in canary_post(), when the event probabilities are large (all subjects with the event, for example).
  • expbern_post() integrates in the same way: for each Gauss-Legendre node of the log placebo rate, the interval of the second coordinate is located separately, and each row is interpolated in the prior distribution function of p or in its normal quantile, whichever gives the faster decay of the Chebyshev coefficients of its density. Before, one interval on the prior distribution function scale of p was used for all nodes, which lost accuracy when the data conflicted with an informative prior of p (cases X1 to X3 of inst/validation/validate_methods_python.R).
  • mapbern_post() integrates over the normal quantile of an envelope of the prior of pi_c when the prior has components with a shape parameter below 1 (total weight above control$eps), as the MAP prior from few historical events has. Before, the integration over the logit of pi_c missed the posterior when the logit densities of such components were nearly flat over a wide range, and prob could be wrong with a small error estimate (cases MS1 to MS7 of inst/validation/validate_methods_python.R). binbeta_post() and exptime_post() integrate over the normal quantile of the prior of the control parameter when its shape parameter is below 1. The coordinate is shown in integration$coordinate; with other priors the results are unchanged.
  • The posterior mean of the ratio of exptime_post(), binbeta_post() and mapbern_post() is Inf when the shape parameter of the control prior (the smallest shape1 of a mixture) is at most 1, because the posterior density of the control parameter near 0 is then proportional to that of the prior.
  • The documentation of llbern_post() says that control$n_outer limits the accuracy when there are many events, and that the error estimate refers to prob.
  • print() shows the tested quantity of the new models and, for exptime_post(), binbeta_post() and mapbern_post(), the posterior of the study drug rate or proportion. Summaries that are not available, such as the posterior mean of multibin_post(), are not shown.
  • The README, vignette("bssd"), the reference index and the articles of the website list all models together.
  • Vignettes vignette("exptime"), vignette("binbeta"), vignette("canary"), vignette("mapbern") and vignette("bdribs-monitoring"); vignette("bssd") lists the methods, and vignette("llbern") explains that the lower limit of the credible interval of the relative risk can be unstable.
  • inst/reproduce reproduces results of Schnell and Ball (2016), Gould and Wang (2017), Brock et al. (2023), Goren et al. (2020) and Waterhouse et al. (2022), and inst/validation compares the new functions with independent Python computations and with MCMC in JAGS.

bssd 0.1.0

  • First version.
  • bdribs_post() computes the posterior distribution of the rate ratio under the BDRIBS model of Mukhopadhyay et al. (2018) as specified by Duncan (2026), with the total exposure time (BDRIBS(1)) or the total time at risk (BDRIBS(2)) as exposure. The background rate has a Gamma prior from historical placebo data (lambda_hp, pt_hp, df), or it is known when pt_hp = Inf (the screening analysis of Mukhopadhyay et al., 2018).
  • expbern_post() and llbern_post() compute the posterior distributions under the exponential Bernoulli (EXP_BERN) and the log-logistic Bernoulli (LL_BERN) mixture models of Duncan (2026) from subject-level data (y, t). For LL_BERN, the relative risk is the ratio of the cumulative incidences at t_star, and the priors of the study drug parameters can be set with mu_d_prior and sigma_d_prior.
  • All posterior quantities are computed by numerical integration instead of Markov chain Monte Carlo sampling. expbern_post() and llbern_post() repeat the computation on a finer grid and report an estimate of the integration error when control$check is TRUE (the default).
  • time_at_risk() computes the total exposure time and the total time at risk from subject-level data. ll_cdf() and ll_mu() give the cumulative incidence and the location parameter of the log-logistic distribution.
  • sim_blinded() simulates blinded trial data with exponential or log-logistic times to the event, and sim_oc() estimates the operating characteristics of the models by simulation.
  • print() and summary() methods for the results (class bssd_post).
  • Vignettes: an overview (vignette("bssd")) and one article for each model (vignette("bdribs1"), vignette("bdribs2"), vignette("expbern") and vignette("llbern")) with examples, the accuracy of the numerical integration and the comparison with MCMC.
  • The folder inst/reproduce reproduces the numerical results of Mukhopadhyay et al. (2018) and Duncan (2026), and inst/validation compares the package with the bdribs package, with MCMC in JAGS and with independent Python implementations.
